newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian G6 to discuss finance market cooperation - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Asian G6 to discuss finance market cooperation - MOF.

text.p: Senior financial officials from five Asian economies and the United States will meet next week in Tokyo to discuss cooperation in financial markets, a senior official of Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Tuesday.

The meeting among officials from Japan, China, Singapore, Australia, Hong Kong and the United States will take place on March 4, and will be chaired by Japanese Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs Takatoshi Kato.
They will also discuss macroeconomic polices, supervision of the financial industry, and possible responses in the event of an Asian version of Mexico's financial crisis.
The meeting is being held at the initiative of Japan, which felt coordination with Asian countries was becoming more important for financial market stability, the official said.

Senior officials from the six economies want to hold such meetings on a regular basis, at least once a year, and hope to upgrade the talks to ministerial level and to include central bank governors, the official said.
They do not plan to increase the membership at the moment and Hong Kong will be separately represented at the meetings even after its return to Chinese rule in July, he said.
Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers will be attending the March 4 meeting from the U.S. side.
